title: Midnight triage heuristic journal (scratch)
content:
Purpose: capture heuristics I use when doing late-night PR triage and quick roll-forwards. Not a policy — just my mental checklist and shortcuts.

Quick context snapshot:
- PR size: small change to batching logic + 1 config flag.
- Observed symptom: production spike in tail latency (~p95->p99) after deploy.
- Immediate ask from pager: revert? patch? hotspot analysis?

Immediate triage checklist (fast path):
1) Can this be reverted ASAP? (yes/no) -> if yes, prepare revert PR + rollback note.
   - Command: gh pr revert <PR_NUMBER> --auto (draft the revert, link incident)
2) Is there a clear metrics anchor? (which metric regressed: token_latency_p99, host_cpu)
   - Pull dashboards: console -> route latency -> filter by model/route.
3) Can we narrow scope to a single config/flag? If so, toggle feature-flag runbook.
   - Feature flag name: batching.v2_enabled (hypothetical)
4) Quick binary search: enable/disable new path in canary region. If canary healthy -> rollout decision.

Safety heuristics (when unsure):
- Prefer revert over partial mitigations if user-facing latency > SLA and root cause unknown.
- If error rates low but latency high, consider throttling concurrency before revert (reduce inflight requests on heavy routes).
- If change touches KV cache keys / cache shape: higher risk for tail regressions -> low tolerance.

Local repro notes (dev machine):
- Repro steps for batching regressions:
  1. Checkout PR branch, run minimal harness: tools/bench/run_short.sh --model gpt-small --seq 1024 --concurrency 12
  2. Use latency profiler: python infra/trace_profiler.py --target localhost:8080 --samples 500
  3. Look at per-layer timing: attention_kv_build, kv_cache_lookup, batching_merge
- If latency increases correlate with batching_merge, inspect buffer flush thresholds.

Patch quick-fix patterns I reach for:
- Offload heavy CPU path to background thread pool for KV serialization (cheap but check locks).
- Reduce default batch size for affected route: config.routes.<route>.max_batch=64 -> 48 (temporary).
- Add short-circuit for single-request fast-path: if request.seq < 64 serve inline.

PR review micro-checklist (what I scribble in the margin):
- Why this change? Is rationale in PR description? (add context if missing)
- Performance assumptions: documented? Include benchmark command and before/after numbers.
- Tests: unit + integration + a small perf test. If missing, mark as follow-up and block if high-risk.
- Telemetry: Did author add metrics for new code paths? (timers/counters/tracing)
- Backwards compat: config flags default to off? migrations?
- Locking: any new mutex/atomic usage? If yes, check contention risk.
- Error handling: does early-return leak resources (buffers / rate limiter tokens)?

Refactor ideas (not for this PR, for backlog):
- Isolate batching merge logic into a pure function with injectable buffer impl for easier testing.
- Add micro-benchmark harness under infra/perf/benchmarks/batching to run CI perf checks on PRs touching serving paths.
- Create an annotation for high-risk PRs that auto-requires a perf smoke report (small load generator run).

Follow-ups to add as GitHub checklist if we revert or patch quickly:
- [ ] Add perf smoke test (infra/perf) for route X
- [ ] Document expected p95/p99 targets in route config schema
- [ ] Add metric: batching.merge.duration_seconds (histogram)
- [ ] Postmortem skeleton: incident timeline, suspected cause, mitigation, follow-ups

Quick decision matrix (mental):
- User impact severe (errors or >2x SLA) + root cause unknown -> revert now.
- User impact moderate (latency but within SLAs) + fix obvious (single flag) -> toggle flag + monitor.
- Low impact or internal-only + fix readable -> patch + canary.

Notes to self (things I will write in PR review):
- "Can you add a short perf section to the PR description with the command used to measure and raw numbers? Without that it's hard to reason about the change under load."
- "Consider referencing INF-321 for telemetry changes so oncall can correlate metrics."
- "If reverting, include a short note in the deploy log so SRE knows why we rolled back."

Fragments / quick thoughts (raw):
- Maybe we should default small routes to bypass batching when seq_len < 32. But that could increase cost.
- Danger: adding more timers increases wall-clock overhead; consider sampling.
- If we add a background writer for KV, watch for GC/pinning in JVM (if relevant).

Edgecases to mention in review comments:
- New path assumes request.metadata.user_tags != null -> NPE? Add safe check.
- Race between flush timer and explicit flush on shutdown -> potential double-send.

Slack threads / links to paste in PR review:
- "see #prod-tail-latency thread (today 03:12 AM)" -> paste graph and note timeframe.
- Link to GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/4587
- Related Jira: INF-321

If I revert, quick revert PR template (copy into GH revert):
- Title: Revert "<short PR title>"
- Body: "Reverts <PR URL> due to production p99 latency regression observed at <timestamp>. Root cause under investigation (INF-321). Revert tested in staging: <link>. Next steps: follow-up perf tests and postmortem."

Sign-off checklist (before closing incident):
- [ ] Confirm revert/pause fixed metrics for at least 30m in canary and global dashboards
- [ ] Create postmortem draft with owner and due date
- [ ] Coordinate with release team for re-deploy window with mitigations

End note: keep this light and iterative. I'll copy the relevant parts into the PR review and into the incident doc depending on action taken.

-- Devon
